questions.question: The cat is running after the rat.(Passive)[]
options: The cat was being run after by the rat.
The cat is being run after by the rat.
The cat is run after by the rat.
The cat is being run after by the rat.
questions.explanation: For Present Continuous, use: Object (The rat) + is/am/are + being + past participle (run) + preposition (after) + by + Subject (the cat)

questions.question: Mend your ways.(passive)[]
options: Let it be mended your ways.
Your ways should be mended.
Your ways are mended by you.
Let your ways are mended.
questions.explanation: This is an advice/imperative sentence. The standard passive structure is: Object + should be + past participle (mended).

questions.question: Who killed the bird ?[]
options: By whom the bird was killed ?
Who was the bird killed by ?
Who was killed by the bird ?
The bird was killed by whom ?
questions.explanation: "Who" changes to "By whom" or stays as "Who" with "by" at the end. For Simple Past, use: Who + was/were + object + past participle + by.

questions.question: He is called a genius.[]
options: Everybody called him a genius.
Everybody says that he is a genius.
A genius calls him everybody.
A genius calls him.
questions.explanation: The passive lacks an agent. In general contexts, "Everybody" is the implied subject. Active: Subject (Everybody) + Verb (called) + Object (him) + complement.

questions.question: He is called a genius.[]
options: People call him a genius.
He is familiar as a genius.
Do the call him a genius.
You may call him a genius.
questions.explanation: here "People" is used as the implied subject. Active: People + call + him + a genius

questions.question: We called him a fool.[]
options: He had been called a fool by us ?
He was called a fool by us.
He has called a fool by us.
He has been called a fool by us.
questions.explanation: Simple Past passive structure: Object (He) + was/were + past participle (called) + complement (a fool) + by + us.

questions.question: He is going to buy a car.[]
options: A car will be gone to be bought by him.
A car is gone to be bought by him.
A car will be gone to bought by him.
A car is going to be bought by him.
questions.explanation: For "going to" structures, use: Object + is/am/are + going to be + past participle (bought) + by + him.

questions.question: Who has drafted this letter ?[]
options: Who the letter has been drafted ?
Whom has the letter been drafted ?
By whom the letter has been drafted ?
By whom has the letter been drafted ?
questions.explanation: Present Perfect interrogative: By whom + has/have + object + been + past participle (drafted).

questions.question: The seat felt warm.[]
options: The seat is warm when it is felt.
The seat is warm to be felt.
The seat was warm when it was felt.
The seat is felt warm.
questions.explanation: This is a Quasi-passive verb. Structure: Subject + was/is + adjective + when it was/is + past participle. Since "felt" is past, use "was felt."

questions.question: Whom is he teaching Geography ?[]
options: Who is being taught Geography by him ?
Is somebody taught Geography ?
Who is teaching Geography ?
Did he teach Geography ?
questions.explanation: "Whom" (object) becomes "Who" (subject). Present Continuous passive: Who + is + being + past participle (taught) + object + by + him.

questions.question: The critic wrote a scathing review.[]
options: A review was written with the critic.
A scathing review written by the critic.
A scathing review written and viewed by the critic.
A scathing review was written by the critic.
questions.explanation: Simple Past passive: Object (A scathing review) + was + past participle (written) + by + subject.

questions.question: We ought to have saved our environment.[]
options: Our environment ought to have been saved.
Our environment ought to have been save.
Our environment ought to had been saved.
Our environment ought to have saved.
questions.explanation: For modal perfects (ought to have), use: Object + ought to + have been + past participle (saved)

questions.question: She does not like eating too much.[]
options: She does not like to have eaten too much.
Eating too much is not liked by her.
Too much eating is not too be liked by her.
Eating is not liked much too by her.
questions.explanation: The gerund "eating too much" acts as the object. Passive: Object + is not liked + by + her.

questions.question: Choose the wrong sentence.[]
options: Honey is sweet when it is tasted.
Honey is tasted sweet.
Rice is sold cheap.
Let a shirt bought for me.
questions.explanation: Option D is grammatically incorrect. The passive for "Buy me a shirt" should be "Let a shirt be bought for me."

questions.question: By whom are you taught English ?(Active)[]
options: Who teaches you English ?
English is taught by whom ?
Who taught you English ?
Who teach you English ?
questions.explanation: Simple Present passive to active: "By whom" becomes "Who" + verb (teaches) + object (you).

questions.question: Which of the following sentences cannot be turned into passive form ?[]
options: He takes exercise regularly.
Open the door.
They are going to market.
He handed her a book.
questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs (like "going") cannot be changed into passive voice because they do not have a direct object.

questions.question: Smoke filled the room.(Passive)[]
options: The room is filled with smoke.
The room was filled by smoke.
The room is filled at smoke.
The room was filled with smoke.
questions.explanation: Certain verbs like "fill" take the preposition "with" instead of "by" in the passive voice.

questions.question: I was obliged to do it.[]
options: They obliged me to do it.
Circumstances obliged me to do it.
Someone obliged me to do it.
A & B
questions.explanation: When the agent is missing in passive, we supply a logical one. Here, "Circumstances" is the most appropriate subject to oblige someone.

questions.question: English is spoken all over the world.[]
options: The world speaks English all over.
The English speak English all over the world.
People speak English all over the world.
All over the world the English speak the English.
questions.explanation: The implied subject for speaking a language is "People." Active: People + speak + English + all over the world.

questions.question: Your blame counts for nothing.[]
options: For nothing your blame is counted.
Your blame is worth nothing when it is counted.
Your blame is nothing when it is counted.
For nothing worth your blame was counted.
questions.explanation: This is a Quasi-passive sentence. These sentences are active in form but passive in meaning. The standard way to change them is: Subject + is/am/are + adjective/complement + when it is + past participle (counted).

questions.question: He knew that his own life was unjust.[]
options: It was known that his own life was unjust.
It was known to him that he was in a unjust life of his own.
It was known that it was unjust his own life.
It was known to him that his own life was unjust.

questions.question: A cat was stalking a bird in my garden.[]
options: A bird was being stalking by a cat in my garden.
A bird was stalked by a cat in my garden.
In my garden a bird was stalked by a cat.
A bird was being stalked by a cat in my garden.
questions.explanation: This is Past Continuous tense. The structure changes to: Object (A bird) + was/were + being + V3 (stalked) + by + Subject (a cat).

questions.question: Why wasn't the matter brought to my notice ?[]
options: Why didn't you bring the matter to my notice ?
Why you didn't bring the matter to my notice ?
Why don't you bring the matter to my notice ?
Why is the matter not brought to my notice ?
questions.explanation: This is a Passive interrogative in Simple Past. To make it Active, we need an implied subject (like "you"). The structure becomes: Why + auxiliary (didn't) + subject (you) + V1 (bring) + object (the matter).

questions.question: Didn't she know anything about the Sundarbans ?[]
options: Was nothing about Sundarbans known to her ?
Was anything about the Sundarbans known by her ?
Was she not known nothing about the Sundarbans ?
Was the Sundarbans known by her ?
questions.explanation: In Passive, "anything" changes to "nothing" to maintain the negative sense, or remains "anything" with a negative verb. "Known" is followed by the preposition "to"

questions.question: She plucked some flowers.[]
options: Some flowers are plucked by her.
Some flowers were plucked by her.
She was plucked some flowers.
Some flowers had been plucked by her.
questions.explanation: Simple Past tense. The object "some flowers" (plural) takes "were" + V3 (plucked).

questions.question: I was deceived by the stranger.[]
options: The stranger deceives me.
The stranger has deceived me.
The stranger had deceived me.
The stranger deceived me.
questions.explanation: Passive to Active (Simple Past). The agent "the stranger" becomes the subject, followed by the V2 form of the verb "deceived" and the object "me."

questions.question: We do not hate the poor.[]
options: The poor are not hated by us.
The poor is not hated by us.
We are not hated by the poor.
The poor is not done to be hated by us.
questions.explanation: Simple Present negative. "The poor" is treated as a plural noun, so it takes "are not" + V3 (hated).

questions.question: Fire burnt the ship.[]
options: The ship was burnt by fire.
The ship was burnt.
The ship was burnt with fire.
The ship was burnt to fire.
questions.explanation: Simple Past. The object "the ship" becomes the subject + "was" + V3 (burnt). In many contexts, the agent "by fire" can be omitted if the result is the focus.

questions.question: Who was helped by you ? (Active)[]
options: Who was helped by you ?
Who did help you ?
Whom did you help ?
Who helped you ?
questions.explanation: Passive to Active. "By you" becomes the subject "you." Since it is Simple Past, the question uses the auxiliary "did" + V1

questions.question: Don't laugh at me.[]
options: Let me be laughed at.
Let me be not laughed at.
I am laughed at.
Let me be not laughed.
questions.explanation: Imperative negative. The structure is: Let + object (me) + be + not + V3 (laughed at).

questions.question: Who gave this book to you ?[]
options: Whom was the book given to you ?
By whom was the book given to you ?
To whom was the book given to you ?
None
questions.explanation: Interrogative starting with "Who." "Who" changes to "By whom." Since "gave" is Simple Past, the structure is: By whom + was + object (the book) + V3 (given).

questions.question: Who gave you the pen ?[]
options: By whom you were given the pen ?
Who were given you the pen ?
By whom were you given the pen ?
By whom the pen was given to you ?
questions.explanation: Here using the indirect object "you" as the subject. By whom + were (matching "you") + you + V3 (given) + the pen?

questions.question: Whom did you know there ?[]
options: Who was known to you there ?
By whom you knew there ?
To whom you know there ?
Who was known by you there ?
questions.explanation: "Whom" (object) becomes "Who" (subject) in Passive. The verb "know" in Simple Past becomes "was known." Note: "Known" takes the preposition "to," not "by."

questions.question: I am to make a telephone call.[]
options: A telephone call is to be made by me.
A telephone call is to making by me.
A telephone call will to make by me.
A telephone call will made by me.
questions.explanation: Sentences with "am/is/are + to + verb" use the passive form: Object + am/is/are + to be + V3.

questions.question: I know what he thinks.[]
options: What he think was know to me.
What he thinks was know to me.
What he thinks is known to me.
He think was is know to me.
questions.explanation: The object is the entire clause "what he thinks." This clause acts as a singular subject: [What he thinks] + is (Present) + known + to me.

questions.question: I was compelled to do it.[]
options: Circumstances compelled me to do it.
compelled to do.
Compelling easy but difficult to do.
He was compelled.
questions.explanation: Passive to Active. The agent is missing but implied (usually "circumstances"). To make it active, use: Subject (Circumstances) + V2 (compelled) + object (me) + to do it.

questions.question: The news shocked him[]
options: He was shocked by the news.
He was shocked at the news.
He was shocked with the news.
He was shocked on the news.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Past, the object "him" becomes the subject "he". Certain verbs like "shocked," "surprised," or "alarmed" take the preposition "at" instead of "by" when referring to a thing or news.

questions.question: He does not like people laughing at him.[]
options: People laughing at him are not liked by him.
He does not like being laughed at.
To be laughed at by people are not like by him.
He does not like him being laughed at by people.
questions.explanation: When "like/dislike" is followed by a gerund phrase, we change the gerund to its passive form: being + V3. The subject "He" and the main verb "does not like" remain.

questions.question: Please grant me two days' leave.(Passive)[]
options: Let me be granted two days' leave.
Let me two days leave be granted.
May I please be granted two days' leave ?
I may be granted two days' leave.
questions.explanation: For polite imperative requests starting with "Please," the passive can be formed using a request structure: "May I + [please/kindly] + be + V3."

questions.question: Nobody trusts a traitor. (Passive)[]
options: A traitor is trusted.
A traitor should not be trusted.
Everybody hates a traitor.
A traitor is not trusted by anybody.
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present negative sentence. To maintain the "Nobody" (negative) sense in passive voice, "Nobody" is replaced by "not... by anybody." The structure is: Object (A traitor) + is + not + V3 (trusted) + by anybody.

questions.question: Change the voice : Kindly grant me two days' leave.[]
options: May I kindly be granted two days' leave ?
Let me be granted two days' leave.
Let two days' leave be granted to me.
Two days' leave is requested to me.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence expressing a request (indicated by "Kindly"). In passive voice, formal requests are often transformed using the modal "May" to maintain politeness. The structure becomes: May + Subject (I) + kindly + be + V3 (granted) + Object (two days' leave).
